eventMetadata.context_description: Latest ensemble forecasts from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts and Météo-France show high pressure building over western Europe, driving clear skies and radiative heating that favor a daily maximum near 24°C in Paris on May 21. Ensemble spreads place the most probable range between 23–25°C, with the 24°C and 25°C outcomes capturing nearly 70% of current trader probability because subtle differences in boundary-layer moisture and the precise arrival of the ridge can shift peak temperatures by 1–2°C. Light northeast winds of 10 km/h limit mixing and allow surface warming, while any residual overnight cloud cover could cap the high at 23°C or below. Updated model runs expected tomorrow will narrow the uncertainty ahead of resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent model consensus from the Korea Meteorological Administration points to a modest diurnal warming trend in Seoul over the next 48 hours, with daytime highs likely settling near 20–22 °C as a weak trough moves across the Korean Peninsula and increased cloud cover limits solar heating. Sea-breeze advection from the Yellow Sea and lingering moisture associated with the early summer monsoon transition are expected to cap peak temperatures, while the urban heat-island effect in central districts may add 1–2 °C locally. These atmospheric factors explain why market-implied probabilities cluster tightly between 20 °C and 22 °C or higher, reflecting traders’ assessment of forecast uncertainty and typical model spread in late-spring conditions. Updated runs and observational data through May 20 will further refine the expected maximum before resolution.

Historical May climatology shows average highs near 21°C, yet current ensemble spread keeps probabilities distributed across the 18–20°C band, reflecting genuine short-range meteorological uncertainty ahead of final observational data.
